subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw accept a direct `gateway.peers` session-tool surface now, or keep cross-gateway messaging behind a broader federation/security design?
rationale: The branch changes gateway trust, credentials, session ownership, and model-callable remote routing, which cannot be safely resolved as a routine code repair.

options.title: Require secure bridge rework
options.body: Do not merge this branch until it uses a maintainer-approved peer or bridge contract, preserves current URL policy, and proves real two-gateway behavior.

options.title: Sponsor narrow peers
options.body: Accept `gateway.peers` as the intended product direction but require explicit security review, docs, and compatibility tests before merge.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open and ask for a fresh implementation after the federation design is decided.

recommendation.title: Require secure bridge rework
recommendation.body: Do not merge this branch until it uses a maintainer-approved peer or bridge contract, preserves current URL policy, and proves real two-gateway behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest ownership signal for the current session tool and gateway URL policy boundary.
